children: According to CNBC, new AI coaching tools are helping managers prepare for difficult workplace conversations, including performance warnings, denied raises and job cuts. A July survey from The Predictive Index found 74% of CEOs and business leaders said their managers are very confident handling tough people conversations, while 42% of managers said they know what they want to say but struggle with how to say it. Only 20% of managers said they prefer to prepare for a difficult conversation on their own, and the survey identified constructive criticism, anticipating employee reactions and staying objective as key blind spots.

Experts said the tools work best as practice and feedback aids rather than replacements for human judgment. Managers can use them to role-play different employee reactions, refine tone and wording, and avoid legal or privacy mistakes by not entering identifiable personal details. Human resources professionals also said managers should still debrief with a supervisor or HR after using AI, since some situations require a human perspective.

title: AI Coaching Tools Help Managers Prepare For Tough Workplace Conversations
